subject: Private deployment: pinning approval runway and checkpoint plan
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Jill Torres <jill.torres@acmeinc.com>, ops@acmeinc.com
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment: pinning approval runway and checkpoint plan

Hi all,

Following up from last week's ops sync — attaching a concise plan for Acme Financial's upcoming private-patch window. This thread is to collect approvals and technical sign-offs so we can lock the maintenance runway and provide Acme the formal 48-hour notice. Key points: 

- Window proposal: Thu 2026-06-03 00:00 - 06:00 UTC (narrow window to minimize region overlap).
- Pinning approach: pin control-plane and worker images to manifest v2 for the duration; manifest is attached (patch_manifest_v2.csv).
- Canary: 5% traffic split to canary slice for 30 minutes, then 25% for 60 minutes before full ramp.
- Checkpoints: immutable checkpoint tags created at three points (pre-patch snapshot, post-canary, post-ramp).
- Rollback criteria: defined in rollback_checklist_v1.pdf — includes performance regressions, KV-cache corruption indicators, and >5% error-rate sustained for >10 min.
- Audit & evidence: Dry-run logs and telemetry for the canary will be archived to S3; we will hand these to Acme for compliance.

Ask: Marissa, can you confirm the comms owner and on-call rotation for the window? Karthik, can you confirm the KV-cache flush compatibility and the exact steps for a safe pin-evacuation if we need to abort? Jill — if this window works for Acme, please confirm and we will send the formal DocuSign amendment and 48-hour notice.

Attachments: patch_manifest_v2.csv, rollback_checklist_v1.pdf, canary_dryrun_log.txt

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Sr. PM, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

---

Note: This message is a planning summary. Detailed step runbook will be posted to the shared drive after approvals.

Thanks — some technical clarifications and additions: 

1) KV-cache and checkpointing:
- We will perform a coordinated KV-cache snapshot before the canary cut. The runtime supports an export of the in-memory KV cache to an immutable S3 artifact; I'll add the exact S3 key to the runbook.
- Flush order: drain reads -> snapshot KV -> pause writes -> apply pinned images -> warm caches on canary instances -> begin traffic split.

2) Artifact pins and manifest:
- patch_manifest_v2.csv includes image digests, kernel/driver pins, and a checksum for the compiled serving runtime. We will verify checksums on every host (sha256).
- Manifest location: https://s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/redwood-shared/manifests/patch_manifest_v2.csv (read-only).

3) Abort / rollback steps (short form):
- Abort trigger -> fail open traffic back to previous model variant -> signal orchestration to pin previous manifests -> restore KV cache from pre-patch snapshot if detect corruption.
- Important: KV restore is destructive for any writes between snapshot and restore; we must capture an acceptance timestamp and notify Acme immediately.

4) Dry-run & observability:
- We'll run a dry-run canary in the staging 24 hours before the window and collect canary_dryrun_log.txt; it's attached.
- Telemetry hooks: token-level latency histogram, worker CPU/GPU utilization, and error-rate per route.

I'll add a short checklist to rollback_checklist_v1.pdf with exact CLI commands and the S3 keys. If we need to add more safe-guards (e.g., automatic cut at 10% error), say so and I'll include the policy in the orchestration config.

Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Hi Laura / team — thanks for the detailed plan. Acme is generally aligned and the proposed window looks acceptable pending two items: 

1) We need a formal 48-hour notice and a DocuSign amendment to the private-deploy SLA for this patching event. Please send the DocuSign link and we will route it internally.
2) Can you confirm the initial canary percentage (you proposed 5%) and the automatic abort thresholds (specifically whether a single route hitting 8% error for 5 minutes triggers an automatic abort)? We'd like these thresholds captured in the amendment.

Also, please include the evacuation marker artifact Marissa mentioned — our audit team will want a single JSON manifest with timestamps and the S3 keys for the snapshots.

I'll sign off once we have the DocuSign link and the abort thresholds clarified.
